samples.summary: Slides is the one collaborative surface left with an ungated load-time `doc.update()` on a read-only mount, so enforce-by-default wedges a viewer's sync
samples.evidence:
This change flips the auth webhook to enforcing by default (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`: anything but the literal `false` enforces) and, on that premise, gates every load-time/presence write on a read-only mount: `pdf-collab.tsx` (`initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`, `onActivePageChange`), `yorkie-store.ts` (constructor presence, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`), `yorkie-doc-store.ts` (`updateCursorPos`, `publishResolvedLocalCursor`), `board-view.tsx`, `slides-view.tsx` `broadcast()`, and `readOnlyNoteStore`.

Slides' *root* path is not gated. `slides-view.tsx:282` calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, …)` unconditionally inside the mount effect — with an in-tree comment that literally says "Known gap (intentional in this PR): `ensureSlidesRoot` may run a `doc.update()` migration block when a viewer mounts an unmigrated pre-v0.5 deck". `mobile-slides-view.tsx:147` does the same, and that is the component `shared-document.tsx:626` mounts for a phone-sized share-link visitor with `mode="view"`.

`ensureSlidesRoot` (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:218-298`) opens a `doc.update()` **unconditionally** at line 246 and writes `themes` / `masters` / `guides` / `meta.themeId` / `meta.masterId` / per-slide `notes` / text `data.blocks` whenever they are absent, plus a `needsRoot` branch at 228 that seeds `meta`/`slides`/`layouts`. `shared-document.tsx:983` passes `initialRoot={{}}` for slides for *both* roles, so nothing seeds the root for a viewer beforehand.

Consequence under the new default: a share-link `viewer` opening (a) a deck whose root was never seeded, or (b) any deck predating `guides`/`themes`/`masters`, emits a local change at load. The next `PushPull` therefore carries verb `rw` (`AccessAttributes(pack)`), `hasAccess` returns false for `link.role !== 'editor'`, and the webhook answers 403 — exactly the "wedging the viewer's own sync" failure the rest of the diff exists to prevent. The attach itself still succeeds (`READ_GATED_METHODS`), so the viewer sees the snapshot and then silently stops receiving anything. The gap was benign while shadow mode was the default (a viewer merely wrote a migration); this change makes it break the read path.

samples.summary: A comment added in this change asserts the opposite of the default the same change establishes
samples.evidence: The new `buildExtensions` comment states: "since the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either." The same change adds `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts`, whose contract is "**Enforcing is the default**" (`isYorkieAuthEnforced` returns true for anything but the literal `false`), and `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:56-67` explicitly retracts that very claim as "wrong". The same now-false statement also survives out of diff at `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42` ("ships in shadow mode by default … with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary"). Both invert the deployment posture a future reader will reason about when deciding whether a client-side guard is load-bearing.

samples.summary: Widening the notes divider 7px→25px without compensating for the grab offset makes the split jump ~12px on the first pointermove
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;` sets the editor pane's basis to `ratio`, which (per the new comment's own algebra) places the divider's **left edge** at the pointer. The painted hairline is the content box of a 25px border-box element with `padding: 0 12px`, i.e. it sits 12px inside the box. So a user who grabs the visible hairline and moves 1px sees the hairline snap ~12px, because the drag math treats the grab point as the box's left edge. At the previous 7px/3px padding the same defect was a ~3px jump; the widening is what makes it visible, and no `ev.clientX - grabOffset` correction was added alongside it.

samples.summary: `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` is cast to `ms.StringValue` unvalidated, so a bad value throws inside the SDK's token-refresh callback rather than at startup
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` does `expiresIn: string = process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` and then `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(secret, expiresIn as ms.StringValue)`; `YorkieService` (`yorkie.service.ts:60-62`) does the same cast on the ConfigService value. The injector body is `() => Promise.resolve(signYorkieServiceToken(...))`, invoked by the Yorkie SDK on activate/refresh. A malformed value (`'900'`, `'10 minutes'`, stray whitespace) makes `jsonwebtoken` throw from inside that callback, where the failure surfaces as an opaque activate/sync error on every server-side attach instead of a loud misconfiguration at boot. The two ops scripts inherit the same path.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. slides-view.tsx:282 and mobile-slides-view.tsx:147 call ensureSlidesRoot unconditionally on mount with no readOnly gate (slides-view.tsx:276-281 even carries an in-tree comment acknowledging the gap). ensureSlidesRoot (yorkie-slides-store.ts:246) opens a doc.update() outside any needsRoot check and writes themes/masters/guides/meta.themeId/meta.masterId/notes/data.blocks when absent, plus the needsRoot seed at 228-242. shared-document.tsx:983 passes initialRoot={{}} for slides for both roles (unlike the role-aware helpers at 974/992/1007/1020), so a viewer's root is never pre-seeded. Viewers reach both mounts: SharedSlidesLayout (shared-document.tsx:404-424) computes readOnly from role and renders MobileSlidesView on phones (419-421) or SlidesView (502-503). Backend premise holds: isYorkieAuthEnforced (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31) enforces unless the literal 'false'; verb is only ignored for AttachDocument (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108, 332-334), and hasAccess (370) denies rw for link.role !== 'editor', producing a 403 on the PushPull that carries the migration change. Net effect on a never-seeded or pre-guides/pre-themes deck: the viewer attaches, sees the snapshot, then their sync is wedged by repeated 403s — a broken read path in normal use. No guard elsewhere skips the migration for read-only mounts. Correctness lane; major/critical impact.

finding.summary: Read-only sheet mount still writes the CRDT root through the cross-sheet recalc path, which the new `readOnly` gate does not cover
finding.evidence: The new constructor comment claims `readOnly` silences "the three writes the grid makes without the user ever running an editing command" (yorkie-store.ts:82-93), but `runRemoteSync(true)` at sheet-view.tsx:1300 runs unconditionally on mount (and again from the remote-change subscription at sheet-view.tsx:1312) for a read-only viewer. It calls `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` → `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2943-2981), which opens `store.beginBatch()` and runs `calculate(...)`. `calculate` writes cells via `sheet.setCell`/`deleteCell` — unconditionally for spill results (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:118-141) and for cycled cells (line 67) — and `recomputeFilterHiddenRows()` (sheet.ts:2976) writes hidden state. `YorkieStore.endBatch()` then issues a real `doc.update()` (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1187) because `readOnly` is not consulted there or in `set`/`setHiddenState`. So a share-link viewer opening a sheet containing a spilling or cross-sheet formula (or a cycled formula) still performs the `rw` PushPull the PR is trying to eliminate — the viewer's sync wedges exactly as before, and if the webhook were permissive the viewer would be mutating the owner's document.

verdict.reason: Every link in the chain checks out. sheet-view.tsx:1300 calls runRemoteSync(true) unconditionally on mount (and again via the remote-change subscription at 1306-1313) even when readOnly is true; the store is constructed with readOnly at sheet-view.tsx:1012 but the flag is consulted only at yorkie-store.ts:109/651/689. runRemoteSync -> sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas() (sheet-view.tsx:1186) -> Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas (spreadsheet.ts:963-967), which notably lacks the 'if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;' guard present on ~35 sibling methods in that same file. Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas (sheet.ts:2964-2979) opens store.beginBatch(), runs calculate(), optionally recomputeFilterHiddenRows(), then store.endBatch() in a finally. In calculator.ts the spill branch writes unconditionally (setCell at 118, 136, 141; deleteCell at 81) with no unchanged-value short-circuit, unlike the scalar (157-164) and cycled (60-66) paths; recomputeFilterHiddenRows writes unconditionally at sheet.ts:1653 via store.setFilterState, which enqueues a batch op (yorkie-store.ts:1021-1031). YorkieStore.endBatch (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1187) then performs a real doc.update() with no readOnly check, as do set (246-277) and setHiddenState (1106-1133). The read-only SheetView is rendered for share-link viewers at shared-document.tsx:283, so this is a normal-use path. The only inaccuracy in the report is cosmetic (recomputeFilterHiddenRows calls setFilterState, not setHiddenState - both ungated). The early return at sheet.ts:2960-2962 limits it to sheets containing cross-sheet formulas, which is exactly the case this path exists to serve, so it does not render the finding defensive or unreachable. Net effect: a read-only viewer still emits an rw doc.update on mount, defeating the gate the change introduces.
